sections.heading: C — Graduated Driver Licensing and application documents
sections.markdown:
## C — Graduated Driver Licensing and application documents

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Graduated Driver Licensing combines two driver education segments with requirements for three license levels, adds privileges at each level, and ends when you turn 18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
You may start driver education Segment 1 at 14 years, 8 months old with a parent’s or guardian’s permission. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Segment 1 takes at least 24 hours in the classroom, at least six hours behind the wheel and at least four hours observing from a training vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Finishing Segment 1 also requires a score of at least 70 percent on the Segment 1 state exam. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
The Level 1 Learner’s License needs a minimum age of 14 years, 9 months, an office visit together with a parent or legal guardian, and passing the vision and health standards. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
For Level 1 you bring the Segment 1 Certificate of Completion plus proof of a valid Social Security number or an ineligibility letter, U.S. citizenship or legal presence, identity and Michigan residency. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A02
A teen given a photo hard card for Level 1 skips the office visit for Level 2, and the regular operator’s license is mailed when that teen turns 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
With a Level 1 license you may drive only when a licensed parent, guardian, or designated licensed adult aged 21 or older sits in the front seat beside you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
A designated adult supervising a Level 1 driver needs a signed authorization letter from the parent or guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
A Level 1 driver keeps a supervised driving log and must reach at least 50 hours, 10 of them at night, before the driving skills test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A02
Kelsey’s Law bars a Level 1 driver from using a cell phone while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
To enter Segment 2 you need a log showing at least 30 supervised hours, at least 2 of them at night, and at least three consecutive months holding the Level 1 license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
Segment 2 includes at least 6 hours of classroom instruction, and its state exam must be passed with at least 70 percent. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
To take the driving skills test you must be at least 15, have finished Segment 2, have the 50 supervised hours with 10 at night, and have held Level 1 for at least six months. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
At the skills test you show the completed log, your Level 1 license, the Segment 2 certificate, and insurance and registration for the test vehicle, and approved driver testing businesses give the test. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
The Level 2 Intermediate License requires age 16, at least 6 months on Level 1, and a record clear of violations, at-fault crashes and suspensions for the 90 days before you apply. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
Hard-card teens who meet the Level 2 requirements and have passed the skills test move up to Level 2 automatically. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
Paper-card teens must visit an office with their Level 1 license, Segment 2 certificate, Driving Skills Test Certificate and the Social Security, legal presence, identity and residency documents described in form SOS-428. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
A Level 2 driver may not drive from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless a parent, guardian or designated licensed adult aged 21 or older is along, or the trip is for work, to or from work, or to or from an authorized activity. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
A Level 2 driver may carry at most one passenger under 21, unless a parent, guardian or designated adult aged 21 or older rides along, the passengers are immediate family, or the trip is for work or an authorized activity. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
Kelsey’s Law forbids a Level 2 driver from using a phone except in an emergency, and a violation could bring a civil infraction with fines, community service or both. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
The Level 3 Full License requires age 17, at least six months on Level 2, and 12 consecutive months with no moving violation, at-fault crash, suspension or GDL restriction violation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
Level 3 is issued automatically and free once the requirements are met with parental authorization, carries no state restrictions, and may be delayed at a parent’s or guardian’s request. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A03
Anyone 18 or older who has never been licensed must apply for a temporary instruction permit at a Secretary of State office and pass a skills test given by a driver testing business. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A03
Adult first-time applicants bring four proofs, covering identity, Michigan residency, U.S. citizenship or legal presence, and a valid Social Security number, and pre-applying at Michigan.gov/SOS speeds up the visit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A03
The written knowledge test is free at every Secretary of State office, or you can take an online version at home for a $6.50 convenience fee. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A03
Your TIP is issued after three steps: passing the written knowledge and vision tests, paying the TIP fee, and having your photo taken. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A03
You must practice with a licensed adult for at least 30 days before the skills test, and after you pass, the license should arrive by mail in about three weeks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A03
The Secretary of State collects Social Security numbers under state and federal law to verify citizenship or legal presence and to help with child support collection. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A03
If you have no Social Security number, you must present an ineligibility letter from the Social Security Administration that is no more than 60 days old. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A03
Accepted proof of legal presence includes a certified birth certificate with a raised seal from a U.S. government unit or territory, a valid unexpired U.S. passport, a citizenship or naturalization certificate, a Permanent Resident Card, or an Employment Authorization Card. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A03
Your first and last names and birth date should match across documents, and every name change needs legal proof such as an original marriage license, divorce decree or court order. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A03
Identity proof must be original documents, photocopies and faxes are refused, and you may need more than one document. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A03
Out-of-state and Canadian applicants may use their own license as identity proof as long as it has been expired for less than four years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A03
Residency proof takes at least two documents, such as a utility bill, credit card bill or account statement from the last 90 days, a pay stub, an earnings statement, a mortgage or lease, or an insurance policy. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A03
Residency documents in a family member’s name are accepted when the family relationship is shown by other documented proof. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0020]
